rows.jp: ……何してるんだか知らないが。
rows.en: ...I had no idea what she was doing.

rows.jp: ヘタにつつくのは利口じゃないしな。
rows.en: But poking carelessly at it would hardly be wise.

ghs.en: poking at stuff randomly ain't clever, no.

rows.jp: それより今の寒気を喚起せし存在が、気になる。
rows.en: More pressing was whatever had called forth that sudden cold.

ghs.en: Rather, the being that is causing this present chill is on my mind.

rows.jp: 家の中に……エイリアンでもいるのだろうか。
rows.en: Was there... an alien in the house?

ghs.en: Inside the house there could yet be... an a-l-i-e-n.

rows.jp: 俺は火炎放射器の一つさえも持っていない、ひ弱な現代ボウイだ。
rows.en: I was a frail modern boy without so much as a flamethrower.

ghs.en: Not a single flamethrower I own, wimpish modern Bowie that I am.
ghs.assessment: 現代ボウイ is a stylized 'modern boy.' 'Bowie' turns it into the unrelated surname of the musician David Bowie.

rows.jp: エイリアンに出くわしても、抗しうる武器などない。
rows.en: If I ran into an alien, I had nothing to fight it with.

ghs.en: Should I stumble across an alien, I have no weapons of any sorts to oppose them with.
Not as long as I have the Fist.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says fists are all he needs. The English begins with negation, producing a fragment that means he does not need something only while he has one abstract 'Fist.'

highlights.text: Not as long as I have the Fist.

rows.jp: 「ついに実戦で用いる時が来たか」
rows.en: “At last, the hour has come to employ it in battle.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Has the time to use this in True Combat finally come?"

rows.jp: カラデ道は、長きに渡って耐え難きを耐えてきた。
rows.en: The way of karade had endured the unendurable for many long years.

ghs.en: I have enduringly endured the unendurable in the Way of Karade.

rows.jp: 空手の亜種としてのそしり・中傷・訴訟。
rows.en: The scorn, abuse, and lawsuits branding us a bastard school of karate.

ghs.en: Calumny - slander - lawsuits place it as a subspecies of Karate.
ghs.assessment: The mock school has endured accusations, abuse, and lawsuits over being a karate offshoot. The English makes those three things actively classify it as one and uses punctuation in place of a grammatical list.

highlights.text: Calumny - slander - lawsuits place it as a subspecies of Karate.

rows.jp: 幾人もの戦友(なかま)が、道を離れていった。
rows.en: Countless comrades had abandoned the path.

ghs.en:
>                                Nakama
Countless Comrade-in-Arms had abandoned the Way.
ghs.assessment: The source says many comrades left the path. The English exposes raw annotation layout and unexplained 'Nakama,' then combines plural 'countless' with singular 'Comrade-in-Arms.'

highlights.text:
>                                Nakama
Countless Comrade-in-Arms had abandoned the Way.

rows.jp: だが人類が地球から根絶されようとしている今、ついに本懐の刻は訪れたのだ！
rows.en: But now, with mankind on the verge of erasure from the Earth, the moment of our true purpose had arrived!

ghs.en: However, in this present where humanity is about to be exterminated from the Earth, at last has the time of my long-cherished desire come!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says 'now, when humanity is about to be eradicated.' English does not use 'this present' as a temporal location in this construction.

rows.jp: 格闘ものっぽいセリフを独白しつつ、階下に向かう。
rows.en: Muttering a line suitable for a martial-arts epic, I headed downstairs.

ghs.en: While monologuing lines suitable for hand-to-hand combat, I turn towards the floor below.

ghs.assessment: いない simply means the person is not there. 'Unpresent' is an extremely rare adjective and cannot stand naturally as this locative fragment.
The Japanese says the person is not in the bathroom. 'Unpresent' is not a locative predicate for a person, and the inverted prepositional construction is malformed.
The Japanese says the person is not in the bath. 'Unpresent' is not a locative predicate for a person, and the inverted prepositional construction is malformed.

rows.jp: 一階の物置部屋……いない。

ghs.assessment: The person is not in the storage room. 'Unpresent' is an unnatural substitute for 'not there.'

rows.jp: 睦美さんの寝室……いない。

ghs.assessment: The honorific is left unexplained, and 'unpresent' does not naturally say that the person is absent from the bedroom.

rows.jp: あ、ホコリが積もってる。
ごめんなさい睦美さん。

ghs.assessment: The Japanese honorific remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 一つ、探していない部屋があった。
rows.en: There was one room I had not searched.

ghs.en: There was one room that I had not searched.
I return to the second floor,

ghs.assessment: The room is directly next to his, not merely whichever other room happens to be closest.
The kinship term and affectionate suffix are left in Japanese morphology rather than represented in English.

rows.en: I put a hand on the knob.

ghs.en: My hand is on the knob.

rows.jp: 入るのは久しぶりだった。
rows.en: It had been a long time since I’d gone in.

ghs.en: It has been a long time since I last entered.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんが、家を出ていって以来になる。
rows.en: Not since Youko left the house.

ghs.en: Ever since Youko-chan left the house.
ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 室内に飛び込むと同時に、演舞！
rows.en: The moment I leaped inside, I launched into a kata!

ghs.en: I catapult myself into the room and at the same time, I dance!
ghs.assessment: 演舞 here is a stylized martial-arts demonstration or kata as he bursts into the room. Calling it simply a dance removes the mock-combat action.

ghs.en: Dust and pride fluttering and dancing.
ghs.assessment: The source says only that dust rises or swirls. The English invents pride as a second thing fluttering in the room.

rows.jp: ホコリの中で暴れたせいか、喉が渇いた。
rows.en: Thrashing around in all that dust had made me thirsty.

ghs.en: Perhaps because of my boastful struggle in the middle of dust, my throat was parched.
ghs.assessment: 暴れた says he thrashed or rampaged around in the dust. The English adds boasting and recasts the comic physical movement as a struggle.

rows.jp: リビングに戻って汲み置きの水を飲も桜庭がトマトを食ってい%Nた。%N※新技術リアルタイムモノローグ使用中
rows.en:
I returned to the living room to drink the water I kept sto—Sakuraba was eating a tomato.
※New technology: real-time monologue now in use.

rows.jp: 桜庭は倒れてもトマトを離さなかった。
rows.en: Even as Sakuraba fell, he never released the tomato.

ghs.en: Sakuraba did not release the tomato even after collapsing.
Sakuraba: "I got sick of curry bread."

rows.jp: 「そこでおまえの家に来てみたら、トマトがあるじゃないか」
rows.en: “So I came to your house and found tomatoes.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Therefore I came to your house, because aren't there tomatoes here."
ghs.assessment: He came to the house and found tomatoes there. The English combines 'therefore,' 'because,' and an embedded question into a contradictory causal sentence.

highlights.text: Therefore I came to your house, because aren't there tomatoes here.

rows.jp: 「だからどうしてうちに来る」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And why did you come to my house for that!"

rows.jp: 「友貴に食料はいらないと言ってしまった」
rows.en: “I told Tomoki I didn’t need any food.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I seem to have told Tomoki that I would not need food."
ghs.assessment: 言ってしまった says he regrettably or inadvertently ended up telling Tomoki he needed no food. 'Seem to have' instead makes him uncertain whether he said it.

highlights.text: I seem to have told Tomoki

rows.jp: 「カレーパンがあったからだ」
その場限りの人生だな。
rows.en: A life lived entirely in the present moment.

rows.jp: 「そういうわけで、今日から厄介になる」
rows.en: “So, as of today, I shall be imposing upon your hospitality.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "And with that being like that, I shall be in your care from now."
ghs.assessment: そういうわけで means 'for that reason' or 'so.' The English expands it into a nonidiomatic nested demonstrative phrase.
The source writes the English word 'why' in katakana. The translation perversely replaces it with the romanized Japanese word 'naze' instead of rendering the intended English exclamation.

rows.jp: 「以上の理由をもちまして、本日より桜庭浩は黒須太一の家に住まうことになった」
rows.en: “For the reasons stated above, Hiroshi Sakuraba will reside in the home of Taichi Kurosu as of today.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "And because of all the aforementioned reasons, it came to be that from that day Sakuraba Hiroshi was to live together with Kurosu Taichi."
ghs.assessment: Sakuraba grandly declares that as of today he will live at Taichi's house. The English changes the spoken present decision into retrospective narration about 'that day.'

highlights.text: it came to be that from that day Sakuraba Hiroshi was to live

rows.jp: 「誰が言葉の意味がわからんと言ったか！　スペペッ！」
rows.en: “Who said I didn’t know what the words meant? SPPEH!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Who said that words don't have understandable meaning! NerNeeer!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi asks who said he failed to understand the meaning of Sakuraba's words. The English instead asserts that words in general lack understandable meaning.

highlights.text: Who said that words don't have understandable meaning!

ghs.assessment: 部屋を貸してくれ asks Taichi to let him use or stay in a room. 'Rent me a room' implies a rental transaction and is not the natural ditransitive construction.

rows.jp: 狂えるほどに正常に狂っている！
rows.en: He was so crazy he had gone right through crazy and come out sane!

ghs.en: I am going insane at how casually insane this guy is!

rows.jp: 「ほ、ほぉ……あの広い屋敷を出てここに住むと？」
rows.en: “I-I see... You’d leave that enormous mansion to live here?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hu-, huh... you leaving that giant mansion to live here?"

rows.en: “Yes. It’s large, but it contains no food.”

ghs.assessment: いいだろう means 'Fine' or 'All right' as Taichi agrees. The English changes acceptance into a question asking whether something is nice.

rows.jp: おぼっちゃまである桜庭に道理を説いても仕方がない。
rows.en: There was no point explaining reason to the young master Sakuraba.

ghs.en: Preaching the truth of reason to Sakuraba the Obocchama is pointless.
ghs.assessment: The class-marked term for a sheltered rich young master is left as unexplained romanized Japanese.

rows.jp: 「部屋に案内してくれようではないか」
rows.en: “Allow me to conduct you to your room.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "How about I show you around to your room then."

rows.en: I showed him to the bathroom.

ghs.en: I showed him to the latrine.
Taichi: "Because it's an eight tatami room."

rows.jp: 「庶民の家なんてこんなもんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's a commonfolk's residence so that's how it is."
ghs.assessment: 'Common folk' is a plural collective expression and does not take the singular possessive form 'a commonfolk's.'

rows.jp: 「おまえの部屋は広いだろう？　やっぱり自宅がいいんじゃないのか？」
rows.en: “Your room is large, isn’t it? Wouldn’t you rather go home?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Your room's big, right? You sure your own home ain't better?"

rows.jp: 「広いといっても１６畳らしいから、ここの倍程度だ」
rows.en: “Apparently mine is only sixteen mats, so perhaps twice this size.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Big you might say, but it's just around 16 tatami, so about twice this one."

rows.jp: なんつう部屋に住んでやがる！
rows.en: What kind of room did this bastard live in?

ghs.en: What sort of room is this idiot living in!

rows.jp: 「感覚的には倍以上なんだが……存外、オレの部屋も狭いらしい」
rows.en: “It feels more than twice as large... Yet it seems my room is unexpectedly cramped as well.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "On first look it look like it should be at least twice, but... seems my room is unexpectedly small."
ghs.assessment: The third-person singular subject requires 'it looks like.'

rows.en: “Put two and two together, would you?”

rows.jp: こいつは霊長類じゃないのかもしれん。
rows.en: Perhaps he was not a primate.

ghs.en: This guy maybe just ain't a primate at all.

rows.jp: 「１２歳の誕生日に、ダディが一番日当たりのいい部屋をくれたのさ」
rows.en: “For my twelfth birthday, Daddy gave me the sunniest room in the house.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "For my 12th birthday, Daddee gave me the room with the best sun exposure."

rows.jp: こいつの家はぜったいオカシイ……と改めて確信する俺だった。
rows.en: I found myself convinced all over again that something was deeply wrong with his family.

ghs.en: This guy's family is totally weird... and my belief of that was renewed.

rows.jp: 「なあ……貴様、小遣いはいくらなんだ？」
rows.en: “Tell me, Your Lordship... How much allowance do you get?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say, bastard... how much's your allowance?"

rows.jp: 無意識に代名詞を切り替えて問う。
rows.en: Without thinking, I had upgraded my form of address.

ghs.en: An inquiry with an unconsciously inserted slur.
ghs.assessment: The narrator notes unconsciously switching his second-person pronoun to the rough 貴様. The English turns that pronoun choice into an inserted slur and omits the actual switch.

highlights.text: An inquiry with an unconsciously inserted slur.

rows.jp: ちなみに俺は甲斐性ある睦美さんのおかげで、月二万円をもらっている。
rows.en: For comparison, thanks to my very capable provider Mutsumi, I get twenty thousand yen a month.

ghs.en: Incidentally, with obligations to the resourceful Mutsumi-san, I receive about 20,000 yen monthly.
ghs.assessment: Thanks to capable, providing Mutsumi, Taichi receives twenty thousand yen monthly. The English invents obligations owed to her and leaves the honorific untranslated.

highlights.text: with obligations to the resourceful Mutsumi-san

ghs.en: The waterline of my living standard's not bad at all.
ghs.assessment: 水準 means level or standard. The English literalizes the word's characters as a physical waterline.

highlights.text: The waterline of my living standard

rows.jp: 誇らしげな気持ちになる。

ghs.en: I felt quite proud about this.

rows.jp: その気になれば、近年価格高騰中のヒットユニ○ン社製レアもの廃盤ブルマー６６７－Ｎ（型番）を毎月一枚ずつ買えちゃうんだぜ！
rows.en: If I so chose, I could buy one pair a month of Hit Uni○n’s rare, discontinued 667-N bloomers, even at their soaring modern price!

ghs.en: If I felt in the mood, I could buy every month one pair of Hit Uni*n manufacture's Buruma-667-N (model number), rare, out of production and with prices known to have sudden jumps in recent years!

rows.jp: そんなフェティッシュなライフを保証された学生は、決して多くない。
rows.en: Not many students could afford a fetish lifestyle like mine.

ghs.en: Students that could maintain a Fetish Life of that kind are certainly not many.
Sakuraba: "It's not like I get all that."

rows.jp: いかに桜庭と言えども。
俺は回転しながらくずおれた。

ghs.assessment: The source writes the English 'really?' phonetically in katakana. The translation leaves a Japanese-accent transliteration and inserts an editorial parenthetical gloss instead of rendering the intended English.
The source writes the English 'yes' phonetically in katakana. The translation leaves a romanized Japanese pronunciation and inserts an editorial gloss instead of the intended English answer.

rows.jp: 「どこの芸能人の息子だ貴様は！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "What entertainer are you the son of, you bastard!
ghs.assessment: The spoken line opens with a quotation mark but has no closing quotation mark.

highlights.text: Taichi: "What entertainer are you the son of, you bastard!

rows.jp: 「第一、オレは芸能人じゃない」
rows.en: “For one thing, I am not a celebrity.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Number one, I am not an entertainer."
ghs.assessment: 第一 is the discourse marker 'first of all,' not a numbered ranking label.

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "As far as I go, I am I."
ghs.assessment: オレはオレだ means 'I am who I am.' The English adds a scope phrase and leaves the complement in an unidiomatic nominative form.

highlights.text: As far as I go, I am I.

rows.jp: 「そーいうセリフは、自分の存在意義に悩んだ末の壮大な自己肯定とともに吐け」
rows.en: “Lines like that are reserved for the majestic self-affirmation at the end of an epic identity crisis!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That line there you should spit out as a splendid self-affirmation after being long tormented by the significance of your own existence!"
That's derailing from the proper course.
ghs.assessment: 常軌を逸している is an idiom meaning abnormal, outrageous, or beyond all reason. The English literalizes it as a vehicle leaving a route.

rows.jp: 「……なあ、家賃として前金で５００万よこせと言ったらどうする」
rows.en: “...Suppose I demanded five million yen in advance for rent. What would you do?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...say, what would you do if I told you the rent's five million, paid in advance."

rows.jp: 「そんなに持ち合わせはない」
rows.en: “I don’t have that much on me.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I don't have that much on hand."

rows.jp: 「……じゃあ、今持ってる金をくれと言ったら？」
rows.en: “...Then what if I asked for all the money you do have?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...then, what if I told you to give me the money you have on hand now?"
Sakuraba: "It's just some coins, you sure?"

rows.jp: なるほど、確かに小銭だ。

ghs.en: I see, indeed they are coins.

rows.jp: チャリチャリ音がする。

ghs.en: There's a jingle-jingle of a sound.
ghs.assessment: The construction redundantly nominalizes the onomatopoeia; the coins simply jingle.

rows.jp: 「はは、おぼっちゃまも貧乏な時があるようだな」
rows.en: “Ha ha! So even a rich boy has his poor days.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hahah, looks like Obocchama has moments of poverty too, then."
ghs.assessment: The class-marked term for a sheltered rich young master is left as unexplained romanized Japanese.

rows.jp: 桜庭は穏やかに笑った。
「まあな。金持ちと言っても、そんなもんさ」
rows.en: “Well, even rich people are only so rich.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Well yeah. You can call me rich, but it's like that."

rows.jp: 「庶民の家の部屋が、こんなもんであるのと同じくな」
rows.en: “Just as even a commoner’s room is only so large.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Same as how rooms are like that in the commonfolk's residences."

rows.jp: ガッ、と腕を交差させた。

ghs.assessment: The two men cross or clasp their arms in a forceful gesture. The passive construction omits both participants and leaves the action detached from them.

rows.jp: 「それに今さら金なんてもらっても、意味ないよな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Anyway, at this point having money is meaningless innit."

rows.jp: 「そういや、おまえには小銭を何度か貸したよな」
rows.en: “Come to think of it, I’ve lent you change a few times.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Say hey, haven't I lent you coin so many times now."
ghs.assessment: He lent Sakuraba small change several times. 'Coin' needs plural or a determiner, and 'so many' exaggerates 何度か.

highlights.text: lent you coin so many times

rows.jp: 「律儀なやつめ。けどまあ記念に返されておくか」
rows.en: “Dutiful bastard. Fine, I’ll take it as a keepsake.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Damn the man of integrity you are. But well, let's say it's returned in memoriam."
ghs.assessment: Taichi decides to accept the repayment as a memento or keepsake. 'In memoriam' commemorates someone who has died and introduces death absent from the joke.

rows.jp: せせらぎの如く笑いあう。
rows.en: We laughed like a murmuring stream.

ghs.en: We snicker together as if babbling brooklets.
ghs.assessment: They laugh together like the sound of a stream. 'Snicker' implies suppressed or mocking laughter, and the comparison lacks an article before 'babbling brooklets.'

highlights.text: snicker together as if babbling brooklets

rows.jp: 案の定、紙幣は入ってなかった。
rows.en: As expected, it contained no bills.

ghs.en: Sure enough, there was no paper money inside.

rows.jp: 十万円金貨が十五枚入っていた。
rows.en: There were fifteen gold coins, each worth a hundred thousand yen.

ghs.en: Inside there were fifteen gold coins, ten thousand yen each.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese specifies fifteen gold coins worth 100,000 yen each. The English renders them as 10,000 yen each, reducing the denomination by a factor of ten.

rows.jp: 「ひぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃぃっっっ」
芋虫のようにのたうちまわった。

ghs.en: I thrashed around like a caterpillar.

rows.en: What the hell was this wallet?

rows.jp: こんなスッゴイの初めて！！
rows.en: I had never seen one this incredible!!

ghs.en: First time I see something this impossibleee!

rows.jp: よく見たら十万円金貨だけではなかった。
rows.en: On closer inspection, the hundred-thousand-yen gold coins weren’t the only ones in there.

ghs.en: Looking closely, they weren't only ten thousand yen gold coins.
ghs.assessment: 十万円金貨 means one-hundred-thousand-yen gold coins. The English again lowers the denomination by a factor of ten.

rows.jp: 昭和天皇ご在位６０年１０万円金貨×８
rows.en: Sixtieth Year of Emperor Showa’s Reign Commemorative 100,000-yen gold coins × 8

ghs.en:
8 x 100,000 yen gold coins commemorating the
60th year of the Showa Emperor on the Throne.

rows.jp: 天皇ご即位記念１０万円金貨×７

ghs.en:
7 x 100,000 yen gold coins commemorating the
enthronement of the Emperor.

rows.jp: 皇太子殿下御成婚記念５万円金貨×２
rows.en: Crown Prince’s Wedding Commemorative 50,000-yen gold coins × 2

ghs.en:
2 x 50,000 yen gold coins commemorating the
Wedding of His Imperial Highness the Crown Prince.

rows.jp: 国際花と緑の博覧会５千円貨×４
rows.en: International Garden and Greenery Exposition 5,000-yen coins × 4

ghs.en:
4 x 5,000 yen silver coins commemorating the
International Garden and Greenery Exposition.

rows.jp: 皇太子ご成婚５千円銀貨×３
rows.en: Crown Prince’s Wedding Commemorative 5,000-yen silver coins × 3

ghs.en:
3 x 5,000 yen silver coins commemorating the
Wedding of the Crown Prince.

rows.jp: 「なかなか買い物に使えなかった」

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I couldn't really use them to do shopping."

rows.jp: こいつ……こんなにあっさり大金を……。
rows.en: He... handed over a fortune without a second thought...

ghs.en: This guy... this much money and so readily...

rows.jp: まさか桜庭の中では……十万円は大金ではない……ではない……ではない……？（エコー）
rows.en: Could it be that to Sakuraba... one hundred thousand yen was not a lot of money... not a lot... not a lot...? (echo)

ghs.en: Could it be that, when it comes to money, inside Sakuraba's head... 100,000 yen are not much... not much.. not much...? (echo)
ghs.assessment: A monetary amount is treated as singular in English: '100,000 yen is not much.'
The Japanese is a startled 'Huh?' The English supplies an adversative conjunction and implies a contrast that is not present.

rows.jp: 人類滅亡前、まだ金が意味のある時代に一度でもせびっていたら。
rows.en: If only I’d hit him up even once, back before humanity disappeared, when money still meant something.

ghs.en: If, before the Fall of Mankind, in the times when money still had significance, I had only just once extorted him some money...
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator regrets not wheedling or begging some money from him earlier. 'Extorted' implies coercive criminal extraction and substantially changes the imagined act.

rows.jp: 神はいじわるであらせられる！
rows.en: The Lord in His infinite wisdom had chosen to be mean!

ghs.en: God exists as my personal bully!
ghs.assessment: The elevated comic line says God is cruel or spiteful. The English turns this into an ontological claim that God exists specifically as Taichi's personal bully.

highlights.text: God exists as my personal bully!

rows.jp: 後悔しまくりの俺だった。

ghs.en: That was the earnest regret spree of mine.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says he was drowning in or consumed by regret. The English piles nouns into a nonidiomatic possessive phrase and adds 'earnest.'

highlights.text: the earnest regret spree of mine

ghs.en: Taichi: "I had enough... let me sleep..."
ghs.assessment: Taichi tells Sakuraba to go to sleep. The English instead asks Sakuraba to allow Taichi to sleep.

rows.en: “Very well. Thank you for having me.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "OK, thank you for the help."

rows.jp: 桜庭は便所にこもった。
rows.en: Sakuraba shut himself in the toilet.

ghs.en: Sakuraba confined himself in the latrine.

ghs.assessment: まあヤツのことだ means 'knowing him' or 'given what he is like.' The English possessive-reflexive predicate does not express that reasoning.

rows.jp: 一晩で忘れてまたどこかに行くに違いない。
rows.en: He would forget by morning and wander off somewhere else.

ghs.en: He'll forget this after one night and he'll be off who knows where, no mistake.

rows.en: The man was a born drifter.

ghs.assessment: 放浪癖 is a habit or tendency to wander. 'Vagabondism' is a marked ideological or social label rather than a natural description of that habit.

rows.jp: トマトは食い荒らされていた。

ghs.en: The tomatoes had been scarfed down.

rows.jp: 一つ残っていたのを食べる。夜食にはちょうどいい。
rows.en: I ate the one he left. Just right for a midnight snack.

ghs.en: The one that was left I eat myself. Just right for a midnight snack.

rows.jp: 「……桜庭か？　もう出て行く気になったか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...Sakuraba? Already feeling like you want to leave?"

ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: リビングに立っていた。
rows.en: She stood in the living room.

ghs.en: She stood in the living room.

rows.en: “What brings you here at this hour?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What do you want at this hour of night?"

rows.jp: こっちの家には入らないよう言ってあったのに。
rows.en: Even though I had told her not to enter this house.

ghs.en: And in my house, when she was told not to come in.
ghs.assessment: The narrator notes that he had told her not to enter this house, yet she is here. The English starts two subordinate phrases, omits him as the person who told her, and has no main clause.

highlights.text: And in my house, when she was told not to come in.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんは……まるで……あの時の彼女みたいだ……。
rows.en: Youko was... almost like she had been back then...

ghs.en: Youko-chan is... just like... like she was at that time...
ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.en: She threw her arms around me.

ghs.assessment: She suddenly clings to or embraces him. The passive progressive turns the bounded action into an ongoing state and suppresses her as agent.

ghs.en: I don't understand this at all.

rows.jp: だが彼女はすぐに身を離す。
rows.en: But she pulled away almost immediately.

ghs.en: She, however, quickly distances her body.
ghs.assessment: She immediately pulls away. English does not naturally describe this as transitively 'distancing her body.'

rows.en: “...There’s a piece of tomato at the corner of your mouth.”

ghs.en: Youko: "...on the lips, piece of tomato."
ghs.assessment: The line needs articles and a finite relation: there is a piece of tomato on his lips.

highlights.text: on the lips, piece of tomato

rows.jp: 彼女の頭部が、俺に合わさってきた。
rows.en: She leaned her face toward mine.

ghs.en: Her head became one with me.
ghs.assessment: She brings her face or head toward his. The English instead claims their bodies merge into one entity.

highlights.text: Her head became one with me.

rows.jp: 唇の端を、舌がかすめた。
rows.en: Her tongue brushed the corner of my lips.

ghs.en: Her tongue latches on the edge of the lips.
ghs.assessment: Her tongue briefly grazes or brushes the corner of his lips. 'Latches on' describes gripping and remaining attached, changing the action's duration and force.

ghs.en: And then, continuing, to the lips...

rows.jp: 到達する前に、両肩を抱いて引きはがす。
rows.en: I caught her by both shoulders and pulled her away before she reached my lips.

ghs.en: Before she reaches, I grab and push her off from the shoulders.
ghs.assessment: The source specifies before she reaches his lips. The English omits the destination and leaves 'reaches' without an object.

rows.jp: こんな不安定になって。

ghs.en: for things to become so unstable.
ghs.assessment: The narrator finds it rare for Youko herself to become this emotionally unstable. The English assigns instability to generic 'things.'

highlights.text: for things to become so unstable

rows.en: Heat rippled through my lower belly.

ghs.en: My lower abdomen ripples with heat.

rows.jp: いつもは強い彼女の、弱い部分に反応して。
rows.en: The weakness exposed inside someone ordinarily so strong called out to me.

ghs.en: It's the response to this weak part of her, who is always so strong.

rows.jp: 「……この家では、しないって決めたろ」
rows.en: “...We agreed not to do this in this house.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...we decided that we won't do it in this house."

rows.jp: 「睦美さんとの約束だったはずだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "As follows from the promise we made with Mutsumi-san."
ghs.assessment: It was a promise they made to Mutsumi. The English uses an unsupported logical formula, says the promise was 'with' her, and leaves the honorific untranslated.

highlights.text: As follows from the promise we made with Mutsumi-san.

rows.en: “And you will keep this one too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And I will have you keep them, too."
ghs.assessment: Taichi will make Youko keep that one promise. The plural pronoun lacks a plural antecedent.

rows.en: I raised my voice and shouted.

ghs.en: The voice raises until a shout.
ghs.assessment: Taichi raises his voice and shouts. The English makes an abstract voice raise itself through a graded process.

highlights.text: The voice raises until a shout.

rows.jp: 「俺の心の中に、まだあるんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It still exists, inside of my heart."

rows.jp: 「この約束が消えたかどうかは、俺が決める」
rows.en: “I decide whether that promise has disappeared.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I will decide whether or not this promise disappears."

rows.jp: 「キミとは他人である、俺が自分の意志と責任で決める」
rows.en: “I decide it by my own will and accept responsibility for it—as someone separate from you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You are someone else. I decide with my own volition what is my responsibility."
ghs.assessment: Because Youko is a separate person from him, Taichi says he will decide by his own will and bear responsibility for that decision. The English instead makes 'what is my responsibility' the object he decides.

highlights.text: I decide with my own volition what is my responsibility.

rows.en: “Again... You always say things like that...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You will now please leave, I hope."

rows.jp: 「キミはこの家に入ってきたらいけない」
rows.en: “You are not allowed inside this house.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You simply cannot come inside this house."

rows.jp: 「……俺なんかに慰められたらいけないよ」
rows.en: “...And you must not let someone like me console you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...it's out of the question for you to be consoled by me."

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんは出ていく。

ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese suffix remains unexplained rather than being represented in English.

rows.jp: 一度立ち止まり、俺の顔を見る。
rows.en: She stopped once and looked at my face.

ghs.en: stopping once to look at my face.

rows.jp: 表情の乏しいマスクはすべらかで、落胆も失意も張りつかない。
rows.en: Her expressionless mask was smooth, leaving neither disappointment nor despair anywhere to cling.

ghs.en: Her mask of scant expressions is smooth, that neither discouragement nor disappointment stick to it.
ghs.assessment: The relative clause cannot attach after a comma with 'that' in this form; it requires coordination or a nonrestrictive 'so ... that' construction.

rows.jp: それでも俺には、彼女がひどく疲れているように見えて、不思議だった。
rows.en: Even so, she looked terribly tired to me. It was strange.

ghs.en: And yet, inexplicably, to me she appeared to be horribly worn out.

rows.jp: 俺は追いつめられたままの姿勢で、冷蔵庫に背を当てたまま、ずるずると床にうずくまった。
rows.en: Still cornered, my back against the refrigerator, I slid down into a crouch on the floor.

ghs.en: Still in the posture into which I was chased, my back slid onto the front of the refrigerator to the floor, until I was nearly sitting.
ghs.assessment: With his back still pressed to the refrigerator in the cornered posture, he slides down until he crouches on the floor. The English says his back slides onto the refrigerator's front and ends with the weaker, inaccurate 'nearly sitting.'

highlights.text: Still in the posture into which I was chased, my back slid onto the front of the refrigerator to the floor, until I was nearly sitting.

ghs.en: Taichi: "What the devil was all that."
